content: coffee A controlled explosion on a film set near the O2 arena in London ignited a fire that destroyed a van and damaged a car and a lorry. Firefighters were dispatched to an open‑air yard on Dock Road in Silvertown just before eight o’clock on Saturday evening. After roughly an hour, with twenty‑five crews on scene, the blaze was brought under control and no injuries were reported. The incident is believed to have stemmed from a pre‑planned filming activity at the location close to the O2 venue, which is scheduled to host performances by Niall Horan and Texas in the coming days. The London Fire Brigade posted on X, stating that the fire at the open air yard in Silvertown is now under control, noting that one vehicle was destroyed and most of a car and a lorry suffered damage, with no injury reports. They added that the fire originated from a controlled explosion on the film set that spread beyond expectations, and that crews worked swiftly to extinguish it and will remain on site for the rest of the evening. The yard in Dock Road lies near London’s cable car link that crosses the River Thames. A Metropolitan Police spokesperson said they are aware of reports of explosions heard in the area surrounding the O2 in Greenwich.
